beats.headline: The skull she carries
beats.text: Katia and I came into this place together. A man we did not know attached himself to us, and when we joined the Daughters he would not be sent away. He took hold of her arm, so I put my trident in the back of his leg. He died of it. The skull over my head is his, and I am not sorry. I kept moving with Hekla. Katia went her own way.

beats.headline: At the controls
beats.text: Half nagini, half orc, Nimblefoot Enforcer, level twenty-seven. One large skull and three small ones over my head, thirteen in all, and I don't want to talk about them. Carl stares at them anyway. I stole the second engine and backed it onto the Vermillion train, and I am the one who can drive a subway car, so I will be at the controls. We are taking the train down to 101 to pick everybody up. Before this I taught economics in Reykjavik, and Hekla was my psychiatrist.

beats.headline: Useful, for once
beats.text: Katia keeps asking what she did wrong. Nothing. She always said she felt useless, and for once she was useful. We were never really going to kill her; we wanted Carl's famous temper to flare. The cat shot Hekla, and in the mess Hekla took one of my hands off in the cab. I have three more. I tell Katia to stop being stupid and come with us. I tell her this is why I left her behind on the third floor.

beats.headline: Katia kills her
beats.text: Hunting Grounds, the end of the floor. Crawler Eva, bitten by a dinosaur and buried in a corner, is still alive, and Crawler Katia Grim goes looking for her. Crawler Katia Grim kills Crawler Eva. That is the whole of it. Two professors came in through the same door; from here on, one. I don't do eulogies, and this is not the entry where I start.
